discovery: Discovery of topological and geometric phases in quantum mechanics (the Aharonov-Bohm effect and the Berry phase)

nominees.name: Yakir Aharonov
nominees.affiliation: Tel Aviv University and Chapman University

motivation: Aharonov (with the late David Bohm) showed that electromagnetic potentials, not only fields, have direct physical consequences: a charged particle acquires an observable phase when encircling a flux it never touches. Berry showed that any quantum system transported adiabatically around a closed loop in parameter space acquires a geometric phase determined by the loop's geometry alone. Together these insights revealed that quantum mechanics carries irreducibly global, geometric structure. Confirmed decisively by electron holography and countless interferometric experiments, they now underpin our understanding of topological insulators, the quantum Hall effect, anomalous velocities in Bloch bands, polarization in solids, synthetic gauge fields for cold atoms, and geometric quantum gates. Few conceptual discoveries have so thoroughly transformed how physicists think, calculate, and design experiments across condensed matter, atomic, and optical physics. Both began from questions others considered settled; both reshaped the field.
